name: WCAG 2.1 Accessibility Heuristics
author: W3C WAI
description: Accessibility-focused heuristics derived from WCAG 2.1 guidelines for evaluating inclusive interface design.

heuristics.title: Perceivable — Text Alternatives
heuristics.description: All non-text content has a text alternative that serves the equivalent purpose. Images, icons, and media have descriptive alt text.

heuristics.title: Perceivable — Adaptable Content
heuristics.description: Content can be presented in different ways without losing information or structure. Supports screen readers, zoom, and reflow.

heuristics.title: Perceivable — Distinguishable
heuristics.description: Content is easy to see and hear. Sufficient color contrast (4.5:1 minimum), resizable text, and no reliance on color alone for meaning.

heuristics.title: Operable — Keyboard Accessible
heuristics.description: All functionality is available from a keyboard. No keyboard traps exist, and focus order is logical.

heuristics.title: Operable — Enough Time
heuristics.description: Users have enough time to read and use content. Time limits can be adjusted, paused, or extended.

heuristics.title: Operable — Navigable
heuristics.description: Users can navigate, find content, and determine where they are. Skip navigation links, focus indicators, and clear headings are present.

heuristics.title: Understandable — Readable
heuristics.description: Text content is readable and understandable. Language is identified, and jargon or abbreviations are explained.

heuristics.title: Understandable — Predictable
heuristics.description: Pages appear and operate in predictable ways. Navigation is consistent, and components behave predictably.

heuristics.title: Understandable — Input Assistance
heuristics.description: Users are helped to avoid and correct mistakes. Error identification, labels, and suggestions are provided.

heuristics.title: Robust — Compatible
heuristics.description: Content is compatible with current and future tools, including assistive technologies. Valid HTML and ARIA roles are used correctly.
